name: Airlite Plastics Co.
old_description: We’re proud of our storied past, but our sights are set on the future. Every day, our goal is to better our process, planet, and customers’ business.
about:
Airlite Plastics Co. operates from Omaha, Nebraska, as a family-owned packaging manufacturer. The company emphasizes its long history while focusing on future-oriented innovation, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The company produces in-mold labeled (IML) and round containers, lids, and drink cups, including oxygen-barrier versions that incorporate an EVOH layer to extend shelf life. Its proprietary FDA-approved resin blends are used across product lines such as cultured foods, household items, horticulture containers, and high-pressure processing (HPP) applications. Decoration capabilities encompass in-mold labeling, flexographic printing with up to eight colors, and dry offset printing with in-house plate production. Engineering services, custom graphics, package design, and marketing support round out the offering.

Airlite serves brands in cultured dairy, household products, horticulture, and temperature-controlled shipping, providing packaging that withstands HPP and cold-chain requirements. Customers range from food processors needing oxygen-barrier containers to horticultural suppliers and consumer-goods companies seeking custom-decorated cups and lids.

The company cites its family-owned structure as a source of responsiveness, avoiding bureaucratic layers to maintain decades-long partnerships. It highlights a track record of pioneering IML packaging, oxygen-barrier technology, and HPP-compatible containers, alongside a sustainability ethos that aims to benefit both the planet and the customer's bottom line.

name: Akrivis Components and Tools
old_description: We supply hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming equipment, wire bonders, DI water systems, and other SMT manufacturing tools.
about:
Akrivis Components and Tools is based in Henderson, Nevada, and was established in 2023. The company was created to provide North American technical sales and support for specialized electronics manufacturing equipment, bridging the gap between overseas equipment builders and domestic manufacturers who need clearer communication, application review, installation, training, and service coordination.

The company does not manufacture equipment itself but acts as a specialized process-equipment distributor and application resource. It supplies hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming equipment, wire bonders, DI water systems, and other SMT manufacturing tools. Its focus categories include cleaning and contamination control, vapor degreasing, PCB/SMT cleaning, lead forming and cutting, lead reconditioning, component tinning, wire bonding, thermal/vacuum heating, and semiconductor packaging support. Akrivis provides installation, training, service, quote coordination, and application review from a Los Angeles-area support point, covering the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

The company serves electronics manufacturers, labs, and production teams in reliability-critical manufacturing, with explicit focus on aerospace and defense electronics and medical device electronics. Customers include those needing precision cleaning, lead forming for aerospace-style requirements, component tinning for defense electronics, and PCB cleaning for medical electronics.

Akrivis was started to address a support gap where specialized equipment categories are too complex for catalog-style distribution and too support-heavy for direct overseas purchase. The company emphasizes an application-first model, coordinating technical questions with manufacturers before quoting, and providing a North American point of contact for post-sale service, spare parts, and factory escalation.

name: Alabama Cable Telecomm Associates
old_description: Founded in 1965, ACBA serves as the advocate for our cable providers, operators, suppliers and programmers.
about:
The Alabama Cable & Broadband Association (ACBA) is headquartered in Montgomery, Alabama, and was founded in 1965. It operates as a trade association representing cable providers, operators, suppliers, and programmers across the state. The organization was established to give the cable industry a unified voice in legislative, regulatory, and taxation matters at the state level.

ACBA does not manufacture physical products. Instead, it provides advocacy, policy representation, and industry coordination for its member companies. Its activities include lobbying, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, and facilitating industry collaboration on broadband deployment and technology issues. The association’s staff works from its Montgomery office to engage with lawmakers, state agencies, and other stakeholders.

The association serves the cable and broadband telecommunications industry in Alabama. Its members include cable system operators, programmers, equipment suppliers, and related service providers. ACBA’s advocacy covers issues such as broadband expansion, spectrum policy, taxation, and regulatory reform that affect the cable sector statewide. The organization also highlights the industry’s economic contributions, citing more than 3,000 jobs and a $3.56 billion economic impact across Alabama.

ACBA was started to ensure the cable industry remained competitive amid rapid changes in technology, information, and communication services. Its stated purpose is to provide members with a unified voice throughout the legislative process and to support the industry’s role in education, economic development, and quality of life in Alabama.

name: Alan Wire Company
old_description: Alan Wire has proudly served and supplied the electrical community as a dependable manufacturer of high-quality wire and cable products for 50 years. Based in Sikeston, Missouri, AW offers copper and aluminum 600-volt wire and cable products for commercial, industrial, and utility markets.
about:
Alan Wire Company operates from Sikeston, Missouri, where it was founded over 50 years ago by Alan Keenan. The business began in the family garage and remains family-owned, with Keenan's sons Scott and Jonathan now serving in leadership roles. The company's Midwestern location puts it within a day's drive of more than 60 percent of the U.S. population.

The company manufactures copper and aluminum 600-volt wire and cable products in a one-million-square-foot facility staffed by approximately 500 employees running 24/5 production. Its product lines include THHN, NM-B, XHHW-2, TFFN, SER, URD, service entrance cable, bare copper, grounding products, aluminum building wire, and aluminum multi-conductor wire for commercial, industrial, and utility applications.

Alan Wire serves electrical distributors, commercial construction contractors, residential builders, utility companies, and industrial OEMs. Its products are used in machine tools, appliances, building wiring, power and control circuits, and both above-ground and below-ground installations.

The company emphasizes an "easy to do business with" philosophy: direct answers, minimal bureaucracy, consistent quality, and a willingness to take responsibility for mistakes. Leadership cites continuous investment in capacity, empowered frontline staff, and a 50-year track record of delivering on promises as key differentiators.

name: Alanic - Wholesale Clothing Manufacturers
old_description: We are the biggest clothing wholesaler and manufacturer since 2004
about:
Alanic, a wholesale clothing manufacturer, was founded in 2004 and is headquartered in North Hollywood, California. The company operates globally with sales and operations offices in Los Angeles, Connecticut, Dubai, Sydney, and London. It began as a clothing wholesaler and manufacturer serving business owners and bulk buyers.

The company designs and produces men’s, women’s, and children’s apparel spanning fashion, fitness, activewear, beachwear, and accessories. Its manufacturing capabilities include cutting, hot stamping, sewing, weaving, and technology R&D, supported by a sustainable production process that transforms waste such as fishing nets and plastic bottles into recycled nylon chips and biodegradable fibers. Alanic also offers complete white-label and private-label manufacturing, customization from client designs, and pre-production samples for bulk orders.

Alanic serves startups, retailers, and private-label brands across the fashion, fitness, sports, and kidswear markets. Its customer base includes boutique owners, sports teams, and fitness communities seeking low-minimum-order wholesale clothing. The company highlights its work with the sports, fashion, fitness, and beach communities as well as retailers worldwide.

Alanic differentiates itself with a versatile catalog, the lowest minimum order quantities in the market, extensive customization services, volume discounts, 24/7 support, and worldwide low-cost shipping. The company states its mission is to “dress the Universe” while pioneering social and environmental responsibility standards in the workplace.

name: Alaska Food Equipment
old_description: Alaska Food Equipment was established 30+ years ago to help Alaskans with their commercial food equipment needs. From the larger retailers to small restaurants & food carts, Alaska Food Equipment has been supplying and servicing all makes & models of equipment throughout Alaska.
about:
Alaska Food Equipment operates from Anchorage, Alaska, where it was established more than 30 years ago to address the commercial food equipment needs of businesses across the state. The company began as a local supplier and service provider, focusing on helping Alaskans source, install, and maintain all makes and models of food service equipment.

The firm supplies, delivers, installs, and repairs a wide range of commercial food equipment. Through a network of shipping partners and equipment suppliers, it can reach customers anywhere in Alaska. A dedicated department works to mitigate supply chain delays, and the company emphasizes that if a specific item is not in stock, it can be sourced. Emergency repair service is available around the clock.

Its customer base spans larger retailers, small restaurants, and mobile food carts throughout Alaska. The company serves any operation that requires commercial kitchen equipment, from full-scale dining establishments to compact food trucks.

Alaska Food Equipment differentiates itself with a 24/7 emergency service promise, a satisfaction guarantee that pledges to stand behind every service call, and a commitment to source hard-to-find items. A specialized supply chain team was created specifically to reduce wait times caused by broader industry disruptions.

name: Albuquerque Apparel Center
old_description: Albuquerque Apparel Center is an infrastructure tailored to meet the needs of designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with a wide range of useful customized products and services.  We are New Mexico’s premier venue of clothing and accessory design as well as supplies, services and events.
about:
Albuquerque Apparel Center operates in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a statewide hub for the apparel and accessory industry. The organization does not disclose a founding year, ownership structure, or founder names in its public materials. It was established to connect designers, suppliers, production houses, and merchants across New Mexico, providing a physical and online infrastructure for the sector.

The center delivers a range of services rather than manufactured goods. It runs a networking hub that promotes New Mexico apparel through events, fashion shows, and multi-media advertising. A physical location allows designers to sell directly to retail customers while accessing wholesale buyers. The online platform NMFashionInfo.com serves as a directory for stores, supplies, services, and events statewide. The center also offers custom design and pattern services, operates the AAC School of Fashion Design with classes in flat pattern drafting, draping, and sewing, and provides mentorship programs. Community initiatives include fashion design classes for battered women's groups and rehabilitation facilities.

Its audience spans the fashion and apparel industry: independent designers, start-up brands, production houses, suppliers, merchants, and students. The center also works with social-service organizations to deliver vocational training. Customers include New Mexico-based apparel companies and individuals seeking education, networking, or promotional support.

The organization states its mission is to foster growth of New Mexico's apparel industry by connecting local companies, guiding start-ups, and providing education. It positions itself as a support system for talent that otherwise lacks infrastructure, aiming to make New Mexico a recognized fashion center leveraging the state's lower cost of living and distinctive Southwest, Native American, and Western styles.
